items.title: Hypolite Charles Interview, 1963-04-13
items.q: The interviewee describes Peter Bocca as 'one of our first class musicians' and mentions him in the context of the Superior band, but does not state a direct personal interaction, collaboration, or membership in a group with Bocca.

ctx.x: Okay, we've got it going now. This is a reel three, Hippolyte Charles, reel two, I'm sorry, Hippolyte Charles, August 13th, April 13th, 1963. The machine didn't work before and I got nervous. But it didn't work. You were saying about Ori and the Crescent Band.

I said the Crescent Band and Ori during those days, that was, you know, that was really getting work. Of course they had a lot of little bands that was playing but they didn't play no music at all. But Ori and the Crescent, Jack Kerrin there, was the only band that didn't use no music at all. You see? But you take the Superior, they had a very wonderful violin player and he was the leader, Peter Bocca. And that's where Bump got all the things that he did there.
Oh he did it? Bump Johnson got them from a fiddler?
